entries.severity: P3 (reviewers disagreed P2/P3; both required it now)
entries.quote: Applying those two transforms to both sides of every content-differing pair yields equal lengths, i.e. the remaining differences - minified identifier names and content-hash tokens - are **length-preserving and net 0 bytes**. So the family is **two behaviour-preserving minifier transform choices**, and no other difference class is claimed. (lines 194-197; repeated at line 348)
entries.corrected_statement: The byte accounting stands, but the length-only inference did not classify the remaining differences. The retained token-level producer measured, over all 389 content-differing pairs of the two retained trees (correction-01/retrieved/products-a0-base and guest/retrieved/products-c-bun): the on-disk bytes match the recorded SHA256 in 389/389 pairs; the two counted transforms account for 8 removed `if(!!` -> `if(` (node 11 -> bun 3) and 8 removed `new Error(` -> `Error(` (node 3888 -> bun 3880) instances, each in exactly 8 pairs, and both are behaviour-preserving; after masking the trailing content-hash filename token (`-XXXXXXXX.js|css` -> `-HASHTOKEN.js`) 381 of 389 pairs are byte-identical; the remaining 8 pairs have equal byte length and differ only in 2101 single-character minified identifier positions (17 distinct directed substitutions, 13 undirected; 2 in property position; 0 keyword/literal/global hits), verified independently by a parse-free byte-run alignment (2101 differing bytes in 2101 single-character identifier runs, 0 runs that are not a single-character identifier). The identifier renames are NOT proven semantically equivalent: no scope analysis was performed, and a globally consistent renaming map is not expected (a first-seen global map conflicts in 5 of the 8 pairs under the producer's stated definition; the Opus cross-review reported 7 of 8 under an unstated definition, a number this producer does not reproduce and does not rely on). The claim 'no other difference class is claimed' is replaced by: no other difference class was measured.

producer output (counts, per-pair token alignment, byte-run records)
human-readable producer receipt

entries.quote: A request without a credential is refused with JSON-RPC `-32602`.
entries.corrected_statement: Withdrawn. The negative probe does not isolate authentication: `guest-probes.py` lines 157-160 send a tokenless `initialize` whose `params` is `{}`, so the request is also missing `protocolVersion`, `capabilities` and `clientInfo`; the `-32602` response has the message `Invalid request parameters` and cannot be attributed to the missing credential. The probe therefore proves neither credential enforcement nor its absence. What the retained evidence does support: the token-bearing `initialize`/`tools/list` path proves readiness of the plugin MCP seam (64 tools, byte-identical surface), and it does not by itself prove an authorization decision for protected tool execution. The authenticated WebSocket comparison in the same report (tokenless handshake closed with 4403; `?t=<token>` accepted) is a separate, valid control and is unaffected. No re-probe was performed.

evidence.role: probe script; negative control lines 157-160, positive initialize/tools-list lines 161-179
case-C receipt: negative control HTTP 200 with code -32602, message Invalid request parameters
backend resolves the caller per tool call (_resolve_caller), so parameter validation and credential validation are separate inputs

entries.quote: The observed message in this round is the ticket-04 classification (`Error: Executable not found in $PATH: "pnpm"`, raised by the file's `spawn` at line 64 through its own `packageManager()` helper path `runPnpmOrThrow`; the shipped tree carries no helper branch).
entries.corrected_statement: The accepted residual is two layers and they must not be merged: (1) in the shipped tree the failure is the test's own helper asking for `pnpm` (`pluginExternalWorkspace.test.ts:27-39` selects `pnpm` unless `npm_execpath` or `NAVIDE_PNPM` names pnpm), so the observed macOS failure is a missing-`pnpm` failure; (2) the Bun `file:` non-optional-peer resolution limit was measured on a withdrawn adaptation path (ticket-04 adaptation-01 correction-01, shapes A-O). Consequence stated for the gate: on macOS the default Bun `test:run` workflow ends with exit 1 (ticket-06 report line 160: `835 files passed / 1 failed; 12,446 passed / 1 failed / 23 skipped / 0 todo; exit 1`), so any CI gate built on it fails until layer (1) or (2) is resolved; user option A accepted this as a documented gap.

limitations: Documentation and evidence only: nothing here changes product source, tests, harness, build outputs or the guest, and no measurement was rerun.
Every corrected statement is a correction of a committed report's text; the committed reports themselves are history and remain untouched.
Evidence SHA256 values were computed at the time this document was frozen; the anchor under checkpoint-B-correction-01 freezes this document pair together with the raw producer outputs.

The F1 classification covers exactly the 389 content-differing pairs carried by the correction-02 pair list over the two retained trees; it is not a statement about every possible toolchain difference.
No scope analysis was performed anywhere, so no behaviour-preservation claim is made for the 2101 identifier substitutions.
